facts.raw_span: 1-week history of painful vision loss and floaters in her left eye
no history of myopia, ocular trauma, or surgery
Visual acuity was 20/30–2 in the right eye and 20/80 in the left eye
intraocular pressure was 21 mm Hg OD and 17 mm Hg OS
mild nuclear sclerotic cataract and no inflammation in the right eye
rare anterior chamber cells, 1+ vitreous cells, choroidal detachments in the nasal and temporal periphery, and an overlying retinal detachment with shifting subretinal fluid in the left eye
no retinal breaks were identified
Laboratory studies (CBC, basic metabolic panel, HIV, T-spot, syphilis screen, and ANCA panel) were normal
MRI of the brain and orbits showed mild posterior scleral enhancement but no intraocular mass
Fluorescein angiography showed late leakage in the temporal periphery
fundus autofluorescence was normal
optical coherence tomography revealed shallow subretinal fluid and a posterior vitreous detachment

concepts.why: The patient's presentation of painful vision loss, choroidal detachments, and retinal detachment, along with the MRI findings of mild posterior scleral enhancement, are consistent with posterior scleritis.
The patient's retinal detachment with shifting subretinal fluid, along with the fluorescein angiography showing late leakage, is consistent with a serous retinal detachment.
The patient's presentation of rare anterior chamber cells and vitreous cells, despite normal laboratory studies, could be indicative of uveitis.

The patient's presentation of painful vision loss, choroidal detachments, and retinal detachment, along with the MRI findings of mild posterior scleral enhancement, could be consistent with Vogt-Koyanagi-Harada disease.
The patient's presentation of uveitis and retinal detachment, despite no history of ocular trauma or surgery, could be indicative of sympathetic ophthalmia.

rationales.F01: Painful vision loss and floaters are common symptoms of posterior scleritis and serous retinal detachment.
rationales.F06: Choroidal detachments and retinal detachment are characteristic findings of posterior scleritis and serous retinal detachment.
rationales.F09: Mild posterior scleral enhancement on MRI is consistent with posterior scleritis.
rationales.F10: Late leakage on fluorescein angiography is consistent with posterior scleritis and serous retinal detachment.
rationales.F12: Shallow subretinal fluid and posterior vitreous detachment on optical coherence tomography are consistent with serous retinal detachment.

frontier_selector.rationale: The patient's presentation of painful vision loss, choroidal detachments, and overlying retinal detachment with shifting subretinal fluid, along with MRI findings of mild posterior scleral enhancement, most strongly supports posterior scleritis, but the lack of systemic symptoms and specific laboratory findings makes Vogt-Koyanagi-Harada Disease a less likely but still plausible runner-up.
